issue.title: plugins: `magpie plugin add`, a backup's restore and a sync replace a plugin of the same package without saying so
issue.body:
plugins/ holds one package per name, so installing a plugin's package from another source (another repository, or git in place of npm) replaces the one installed (store.go's add, behind plugin.Add and plugin.AddExact: `x.Spec == spec || n == name`, store.go:474; lines at f8cd964a). Its options, Off and provider picks carry over, and since sign-ins are kept by provider id, the new code gets the old one's saved sign-ins for every provider they share.

The patch I'm posting on #3685 makes the Plugins page's Install ask first. These still replace without saying so:

- `magpie plugin add github:B/foo` with github:A/foo, or npm's foo, installed prints `✓ added github:B/foo` (internal/cli/plugins_cli.go:62), then the list, without A. Nothing says A was replaced. The CLI already adds a line when a typed name was taken for a community plugin (plugins_cli.go:64-65); a "replaced github:A/foo" line would fit there.
- provider.AddPlugins, which a backup's restore and a sync use, says it "never takes a plugin away or changes one already here" (provider/backup.go:172-173). It checks what's here by plugin.Name (176-182), and a git spec this computer hasn't installed is its own Name (store.go:369-373). So a carried github:B/foo isn't here beside a local github:A/foo or npm's foo of the same package, and plugin.AddExact replaces the local one. The restore then prints "Plugins added: github:B/foo" (cli/backup_cmd.go:126), and a sync logs only failures (davsync.go:979-983).
- The page's field ("Have one in mind?") given a bare name, which resolve may take for a community plugin's, or a repository the page hasn't read: the page can't know the package before it's installed, so the patch leaves these as they were.

I checked the restore's part with a test against internal/plugin's fake bun: a carried github:other/repo took github:owner/repo's place and kept its Off and options. I haven't run a real restore or sync.

comments.body:
The cause: `plugins/` holds one package per name, and `plugin.add` takes the entry it matches by `x.Spec == spec || n == name` (internal/plugin/store.go). `provider.AddPlugins`, which a backup's restore and a sync go through, skipped what was here by `plugin.Name(e.Spec)` — and a git spec this computer hasn't installed is its own name (`gitName`) — so a carried `github:B/foo` got past that check and replaced the local `github:A/foo` or npm's `foo`, and nothing said so on any of the three paths.

The branch keeps that replacement (one package is one entry; its Off, options and provider picks carry over as before) and says it. `provider.AddPlugin` gives back the spec its install replaced, `provider.AddPlugins` gives the replacements as new spec → old spec, and `backup.Result` carries them. `magpie plugin add` prints `replaced github:A/foo`, a restore prints `Plugins replaced: github:A/foo → github:B/foo` in the CLI and in the window's import (with its Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese and German), and a sync logs `sync: plugin github:B/foo replaced github:A/foo` where it logged only failures.

[fix/3927-plugins-magpie-plugin-add-a](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3927-plugins-magpie-plugin-add-a), commit 0aecbae86030f286b8fa0b0ca17d41361e045433

Run: `TestAddPluginsNamesThePluginItReplaced` (internal/provider) — with the reporting taken out it fails `replaced map[], want npm's spec that the repository's package took the place of`, and passes with the change (it stubs bun's install the way `bun add` leaves `plugins.json` and `plugins/package.json`). `gofmt -l` on the changed files prints nothing; `go build ./...`, `GOOS=windows go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` are clean; the provider, backup, davsync, cli and gui suites pass except `TestCodexAppServersOnHome`, which fails the same on upstream/main's code on this machine. The import's line was checked in Chromium and WebKit, en/zh/zh-TW/ja/de, 1100/900/440/420px. Not tried: a real `magpie plugin add`, restore or sync against a live bun install.

This is a fork branch, ready to review — not a claim on the issue.

issue.title: 插件页把「同名不同仓库」的 fork 也标成「已安装」，出现两张已安装卡片

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**现象**

我只装了一个插件：`github:mu-zi-lee/magpie-our-free-model`。但插件页（`?view=plugins`）里出现了**两张卡片，都写着「已安装」**：

- `mu-zi-lee/magpie-our-free-model`（package `magpie-our-free-model`）—— 这个是真装了的
- `Gyarados4157/magpie-our-free-model` —— 另一个仓库，package 也叫 `magpie-our-free-model`

其实只装了一个：`/config/magpie/plugins.json` 里只有 `github:mu-zi-lee/magpie-our-free-model`，磁盘上没有 Gyarados4157 的任何东西。所以第二张的「已安装」是错的，看着像装了两个。

**原因（看了 `internal/gui/assets/plugins.js`）**

判断「已安装」的 `entryOf` 是这段：

```js
const entryOf = (pkg) => {
  const g = (tagged || []).find((x) => x.package === pkg)?.github;
  return mine?.plugins?.find((e) =>
    name(e.spec) === pkg ||
    (g && (ghRepo(e.spec) === g.repo.toLowerCase() ||
           (g.package && isGit(e.spec) && e.package === g.package))));
};
```

第三种情况 `e.package === g.package` 的意思是「只要 package.json 里声明的包名一样，就算同一个插件」。两个仓库包名都叫 `magpie-our-free-model`，于是 Gyarados4157 那张卡就匹配到了已安装的 mu-zi-lee 条目，被标成「已安装」。

另外，GitHub 区去重只排除了「包名已经在官方清单里」的仓库，并没有在两个 GitHub 仓库之间按包名互相去重：

```js
const listed = new Set(listings.map((l) => l.package));
const gh = (tagged || []).filter((l) => !(l.github.package && listed.has(l.github.package)) && match(l));
```

所以两个同名仓库都会留下来，各渲染一张卡片。

**期望**

- 只有「这个仓库本身」被装了，才显示「已安装」，而不是「别人声明了相同的包名」也显示已安装。
- 两个同名仓库不应该都被当成已安装。

**为什么在意**

同名不同作者很容易混淆、甚至仿冒。把 fork 标成「已安装」，会让人误以为它就是同一个、可以放心点；而且如果在那张卡上点更新/安装，可能把安装来源从 `github:mu-zi-lee/...` 悄悄换成 `github:Gyarados4157/...`。

**复现**

1. 安装 `github:mu-zi-lee/magpie-our-free-model`（包名 `magpie-our-free-model`）。
2. 存在另一个打了 `magpie-plugin` 标签、包名相同的仓库（这里是 `Gyarados4157/magpie-our-free-model`）。
3. 打开插件页 → 两张卡都显示「已安装」。

**环境**

- magpie v0.1.1564（Docker，Linux）

issue.title: Sign-ins sync (`WithSignIns` / `signIns:true`) copies single-use rotating refresh tokens to a second computer, where both machines race to refresh and the loser is signed out for good

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

A MiniMax Code account (`@magpie-community/opencode-minimax-auth`, both `minimax-code` and `minimax-code-global`) needs a fresh device sign-in roughly once a day once sign-ins are included in magpie's sync. It does not recover on its own: `logins.json` marks the account `lapsed`, `plugin-auth.json` still holds the old tokens, and every `auth.refresh`, `provider.models` and daily check-in keeps failing until a human signs in again.

The same happens to a Qoder account over the same period. Accounts whose credentials are long-lived (zcode, workbuddy) are unaffected.

This is **not** "the vendor's access token is short-lived". Short `expires_in` is expected and the plugin is built for it: `auth.refresh` with `refreshLead = 10 min` renews ahead of expiry, and a 401 force-refreshes and retries. The failure is that the *refresh itself* is refused.

## Why

MiniMax Code (and Qoder / Trae) spend a refresh token **once**: a refresh returns a new refresh token and invalidates the old one. Replaying the old one answers `HTTP 400 invalid_grant`. The plugin treats exactly that as fatal:

```js
const signedOut = (e) => e instanceof OAuthError && e.code === "invalid_grant" && e.httpStatus === 400
// -> new SignInExpired(site)  ("this MiniMax Code account is signed out; sign in again")
```

MiniMax's own client serialises this with a cross-process lock plus a generation counter. In magpie:

1. `WithSignIns` / `signIns:true` deliberately puts `plugin-auth.json` into the sealed backup so that "another computer comes out signed in" (`internal/backup/signins_carry_test.go`). That is a sensible feature for **copyable** credentials (API keys, long-lived JWTs, zcode's self-contained JSON state).
2. For a single-use refresh token, copying means *two owners of one token*. It is not a copy, it is a race. Both machines call `auth.refresh` at `expires - refreshLead` — and magpie calls `auth.refresh` for **every** plugin account on startup, whether the account is used or not — so the second machine spends the token even if it never sends a single request to that provider.
3. The loser gets `invalid_grant`, is marked signed out, and there is no self-heal: `fresh()` can only recover if a *newer* refresh token has already reached its auth store, and sync does not bring it back in time (it runs on `autoEvery: 60`).
4. Re-signing in on the winner produces a new generation, sync carries it over, and the cycle repeats on the next token lifetime — hence "about once a day".

Auto-restart (`autoRestart: true`, hourly update checks) makes this worse: each restart starts a new plugin host that re-reads the store, and the plugins only deduplicate refreshes **within one process** (`renewing` / `renewed` maps in `index.mjs`). There is no cross-process lock.

## Evidence (all credentials redacted; only token *fingerprints* compared)

| When (UTC+8) | What |
| --- | --- |
| before 2026-11-04 19:45 | No minimax errors at all in `app.log` (log starts 10-31); remote sync backups up to 10-20 contain **no** `signIns` section |
| 2026-11-04 19:45 | Sign-ins sync enabled (`sync.json`: `keys:true, signIns:true, autoEvery:60`); the account is re-signed in at the same instant |
| 2026-11-04 20:47 | First `auth.refresh: this MiniMax Code account is signed out; sign in again` — about an hour later |
| 2026-11-04 23:06 | First remote backup carrying `signIns.plugins['minimax-code']` |
| 2026-11-05 00:00, 11-06 00:00 | Daily check-ins still succeed (`+400`, streak 2 and 3), so the chain stayed alive between re-logins |
| 2026-11-06 15:25:14 | `auth.refresh` fails again — exactly 10 minutes before the stored `expires` of 15:35:14, i.e. the scheduled `refreshLead` renewal, not a natural expiry |
| 2026-11-06 15:25 → 11-07 10:41 | The same error every ~30-60 min, ~90 times; all check-ins fail |

The sealed sync backups show **two different refresh-token fingerprints** for the same account (one in the 11-04 backup, another in the 11-07 backup / local `plugin-auth.json`), i.e. the credential really did change generations inside the sync path. A second computer is active on the same sync target during those days (its usage data runs through 11-06) although it never issues a single request to `minimax-code` — consistent with magpie renewing every account on startup.

Corroboration: the Qoder account reports `qoder job token refresh: status 401` continuously over the same window; zcode/workbuddy accounts, whose refresh tokens are long-lived, never do. The dividing line is "does the refresh token rotate", not "is the account synced".

## Minimal repro

1. Two computers share one WebDAV sync target, both with `signIns:true` (`WithSignIns`) and `autoEvery:60`; both run the minimax-code plugin.
2. Sign in to MiniMax Code on A; let sync carry the sign-in to B (or restore a keyed backup with sign-ins on B).
3. Leave both magpie instances running. Startup on B already calls `auth.refresh` for the account it never uses.
4. At `expires - refreshLead`, both spend the same refresh token. One rotates to a new generation; the other gets `400 invalid_grant` → `SignInExpired` → `lapsed`, with no recovery short of a device sign-in.
5. Re-sign in on A, sync, repeat on the next lifetime.

## Suggested fix

In order of how local the change is:

1. **Let a credential declare that it cannot be shared.** A plugin-side flag on the auth (e.g. `rotating: true` / `nonTransferable: true`, alongside `refreshLead`) that `WithSignIns`, restore and sync honour: exclude those accounts by default, or at least warn in the UI that "this sign-in cannot be shared with another computer". A per-account / per-provider **"this computer only"** switch would fit the same shape as the per-agent switches in #4648. This keeps the VPS-restore feature that motivated `WithSignIns` intact for everyone else.
2. **Make sync generation-aware.** Track a per-account credential fingerprint, accept only a *newer* generation, never write an older one back, and surface a divergence instead of silently replacing. Today a stale generation can be restored over a live one.
3. **Self-heal on `invalid_grant` in the host.** Before declaring a plugin sign-in lapsed, re-read the auth store / re-fetch from sync once and retry with the newer token if one appeared. The plugin already has this path (`now.refresh !== a.refresh`), but nothing delivers the newer generation to it. Related: #5080 covers renewing *idle* accounts on a timer; this is the other half — renewing them from two places at once. #1674 (a read-only CLI rewriting `logins.json` over a refreshed token, no lock) is the same class of hazard on the built-in store.

## Workaround in use

Turn `signIns` off on both computers, keep the rotating-token accounts signed in on one machine only, and sign in once more there. Verified hypothesis so far: if the account survives several token lifetimes with sync off, the server's short `expires_in` is not the cause.

## Environment

magpie 0.1.3214, Windows; `@magpie-community/opencode-minimax-auth` 0.2.3; `@magpie-community/opencode-qoder-auth`; WebDAV sync with `signIns:true, keys:true, autoEvery:60`; `autoRestart:true`, `updateEvery:60`.

Related: #5080, #1674, #3927, #4917.
